## Natural history notes

A medium-sized bagworm moth characterized by the caterpillar’s portable, spindle-shaped silk case covered with bits of leaves, bark, twigs, and other plant material. In Florida, it is found in forests, hammocks, pine flatwoods, parks, gardens, yards, and other wooded or landscaped habitats where suitable trees and shrubs occur. The caterpillars feed on foliage while carrying their camouflaged cases, while adult males are winged moths that fly to find females, which remain larva-like and stay within the protective bag.
